Exploration vs Exploitation
•  Exploration: Choosing untested or seemingly suboptimal actions to discover more
   information about the environment, which may reveal better long-term strategies.
•  Exploitation: Agent selects the best-known action based on current value
   estimates to achieve the highest immediate reward.
•  The Core Challenge in RL: An agent must balance this trade-off. Leaning too far in
   either direction leads to failure:
   ꟷToo much exploitation: The agent risks getting stuck in a suboptimal strategy (local
      minimum) because it never tries new things that might be better.
   ꟷToo much exploration: The agent fails to collect significant
       cumulative rewards, as it constantly tests random actions.
   ꟷThe goal is to find a balanced trade-off between gathering
      new information and utilizing its existing knowledge
        to maximize cumulative rewards over the long term.

concepts.title: Learning signals across three paradigms
concepts.description: The comparison concerns the source of learning guidance, not a claim that these are the only possible learning categories.

concepts.title: Teacher versus critic and dense feedback
concepts.description: The source’s frequent scarcity/delay description is not universal: the FetchReach dense reward evaluates distance at each step.
concepts.subtopic: Teacher versus critic and dense feedback

concepts.title: Agent–environment diagram
concepts.description: The agent acts, the environment changes, and feedback informs the next decision.

concepts.title: Agent and environment boundary
concepts.description: The agent is the decision-maker; the environment is what it interacts with outside the chosen modeling boundary.

concepts.title: Discrete and continuous action sets
concepts.description: The modeled action set, not the physical continuity of the robot’s trajectory, determines the distinction.

concepts.title: State is not always fully observed
concepts.description: A complete modeled state and the information actually sensed by the agent need not coincide.
concepts.subtopic: State is not always fully observed

concepts.title: Transition timing
concepts.description: The chosen action at time t produces the successor state and its associated next reward/observation.

concepts.title: Episode boundary and continuing tasks
concepts.description: Under the explicitly stated continuing-task premise, a 50-step collection boundary can truncate a trajectory without a natural terminal state. As an external API qualification, FetchReachDense-v4 in Gymnasium 1.4.0/Gymnasium-Robotics 1.4.2 has this continuing-task behavior; see the linked implementation evidence, not the slide’s episodic wording.

concepts.title: Deterministic and stochastic policies
concepts.description: Determinism means one specified action per given state, not one action for the entire task.

concepts.title: Observed reward, greedy bootstrap and sampled next action
concepts.description: The reward 2 is observed, but both continuation values are estimates. Q-learning targets 2+0.9×4=5.6 regardless of the exploratory next action; Sarsa targets 2+0.9×1=2.9 for the selected B. Neither complete bootstrapped target is an observed full return.

concepts.title: Off-policy does not remove data requirements
concepts.description: Off-policy identifies whose policy is being learned; adequate state-action sampling and other conditions remain necessary for classical guarantees.
concepts.subtopic: Off-policy does not remove data requirements

concepts.title: Finite undiscounted return
concepts.description: The finite undiscounted expression sums every included future reward without averaging or discounting.

concepts.title: Discount powers start at zero
concepts.description: The first reward has weight γ^0 = 1; later rewards have successively smaller powers.

concepts.title: Meaning of the discount factor
concepts.description: Discounting and exploration are different mechanisms: γ weights future reward while ε controls the behavior policy.

concepts.title: Bounded infinite reward series
concepts.description: An infinite number of rewards can have a finite discounted sum; no hard time cutoff is needed for this bounded example.

concepts.title: Optimal state value and action value
concepts.description: The first action is constrained in Q*, whereas V* also optimizes that first choice.
concepts.subtopic: Optimal state value and action value

concepts.title: Optimality is in expectation
concepts.description: The expectation in the source is essential; it does not promise the same or best realized outcome on every trial.

concepts.title: First reward plus discounted tail
concepts.description: The discounted sum is recursively r_(t+1) + γ G_(t+1); conditioning and optimal continuation yield the Bellman equations.

concepts.title: Transition model in Bellman expectations
concepts.description: The transition model weights next-state values in an expected continuation return.

concepts.title: Expected Bellman backup
concepts.description: Environment outcomes are probability-weighted; the agent does not choose which random successor occurs.

concepts.title: Next action may depend on observed successor
concepts.description: The Bellman action maximum is inside the next-state expectation because the later decision can use the later state.
concepts.subtopic: Next action may depend on observed successor

concepts.title: Greedy policy and tied values
concepts.description: Argmax can be a set. A particular implementation may choose one tied maximizer, but uniqueness is not implied.

concepts.title: Exploitation uses estimated return
concepts.description: Q values summarize discounted cumulative reward; exploitation of them need not be myopic.

concepts.title: Exploration and exploitation tradeoff
concepts.description: Exploration trades some current performance for information; too little can preserve a mistaken preference.

concepts.title: Known-model planning versus model-free learning
concepts.description: The known-model dynamic-programming example should not be generalized to every model-based method.

concepts.title: Target, error and update
concepts.description: The update adds α times target-minus-estimate; reward and successor are sampled, while the future Q term remains estimated.

concepts.title: One Q-learning update
concepts.description: A learning rate of 0.1 moves the old estimate one tenth of the way toward the target.

concepts.title: A learning-rate statement is not a convergence proof
concepts.description: The classical tabular result requires suitable state/action coverage and learning rates such as Σα=∞ and Σα²<∞ along each updated pair, together with its finite discounted Markov-task assumptions. The fixed α=0.1 demonstration does not establish those hypotheses.
concepts.subtopic: A learning-rate statement is not a convergence proof

concepts.title: Q table and episode initialization
concepts.description: Per-episode state reset is distinct from global value-table initialization.

concepts.title: Exploration branch probability versus action probability
concepts.description: ε is the probability of entering the random branch, not the probability of choosing a non-greedy action.
concepts.subtopic: Exploration branch probability versus action probability

concepts.title: Reaching is not the whole grasping task
concepts.description: The slide draws reaching followed by closing the gripper. That schematic does not prove every target is feasible or that the later FetchReach task includes grasping.
concepts.subtopic: Reaching is not the whole grasping task

concepts.title: Gymnasium’s responsibility
concepts.description: Standard methods such as reset and step support experiments, while the supplied code implements learning.

concepts.title: MuJoCo and simulation scope
concepts.description: The source’s manipulation, navigation and humanoid examples illustrate simulation scope, not guaranteed real-world transfer.

concepts.title: Robot joints versus action coordinates
concepts.description: The source uses [dx,dy,dz,gripper] as a high-level task-space interface, rather than one independent policy coordinate for each arm joint. Action-interface dimension and mechanical degrees of freedom need not match.

concepts.title: Negative Euclidean goal distance
concepts.description: Closer is better because a smaller nonnegative distance produces a larger, less negative reward.

concepts.title: Nonpositive is not strictly negative
concepts.description: The source’s “always negative” wording should be read as nonpositive for the displayed negative-distance function.

concepts.title: Import, registration and environment construction
concepts.description: Registration makes identifiers available; construction creates the selected environment. The installed-source check records that import registers tasks and the compatibility register_envs helper is a no-op in Gymnasium 1.4.0.

concepts.title: Notebook installation syntax
concepts.description: The source is notebook-oriented and unpinned. Our compatibility pin is explicitly added reproduction context, not silently attributed to this command.

concepts.title: Six discrete choices through a continuous interface
concepts.description: The agent selects a finite subset of vectors accepted by a continuous four-dimensional environment action space.
concepts.subtopic: Six discrete choices through a continuous interface

concepts.title: Normalized command is not achieved distance
concepts.description: The environment interprets normalized controls; the bin size only participates in encoding the observed goal error.
concepts.subtopic: Normalized command is not achieved distance

concepts.title: Table dimensions and storage
concepts.description: The three grid axes index states; the last axis holds one value per discrete action.

concepts.title: Raw Q-array memory
concepts.description: Array dtype determines bytes per entry. ACTION_MAP’s explicit float32 does not change the separately created Q array’s default float64 dtype.

concepts.title: What get_state encodes
concepts.description: The source’s position wording is incomplete: it is a relative target-minus-achieved encoding.

concepts.title: Calculating encoded goal error
concepts.description: The code shifts each error coordinate, scales by the bin size, converts toward zero, then clips. These positive scaled values yield (5,3,4).

concepts.title: Zero goal error is the central bin
concepts.description: A zero physical error does not mean a zero array index because the encoding includes an offset.
concepts.subtopic: Zero goal error is the central bin

concepts.title: Clipping and state aliasing
concepts.description: The finite encoding is a lossy abstraction; it trades detail for a manageable table.

concepts.title: A grid tuple is not automatically Markov
concepts.description: The code’s compressed state is an approximation. Markov sufficiency must be justified from the task, not inferred from having a Q table.
concepts.subtopic: A grid tuple is not automatically Markov

concepts.title: Reset return values and persistent learning
concepts.description: Environment reset and learner-memory reset are separate operations.
concepts.subtopic: Reset return values and persistent learning

concepts.title: Tie-breaking and epsilon branch
concepts.description: The action selection is not random tie-breaking on the greedy branch; zero initialization initially favors index 0 when that branch is used.

concepts.title: Greedy choice among negative values
concepts.description: With negative rewards, less negative estimated return is preferable under maximization.

concepts.title: Five outputs of step
concepts.description: The observation and reward are followed by two distinct stopping indicators and auxiliary information.

concepts.title: Terminated does not mean won
concepts.description: The source’s “won” explanation is too narrow. The linked installed-code audit checks the continuing FetchReachDense-v4 task, its always-false task termination and the default 50-step TimeLimit wrapper. The saved 5000-segment author run corroborates that setup, with zero terminations and 5000 truncations; it is not independent verification or a universal statement about every task.

concepts.title: First update from a zero table
concepts.description: Only the chosen state-action entry is moved toward the negative target.
concepts.subtopic: First update from a zero table

concepts.title: Update with a negative continuation estimate
concepts.description: Subtracting a negative old estimate matters: the error is −0.069−(−0.01)=−0.059.
concepts.subtopic: Update with a negative continuation estimate

concepts.title: State advancement after the update
concepts.description: The target is 1+0.9×7=7.3, so Q[S,a] becomes 5+0.1(7.3−5)=5.23. The write belongs to the old source pair; a saved old-state variable permits equivalent ordering, but forgetting S does not.

concepts.title: True terminal update versus truncation
concepts.description: For true termination, target is reward alone. For an external time-limit truncation of continuing FetchReach, bootstrapping remains appropriate. The source code does not distinguish these cases in its update.

concepts.title: Undiscounted logged total versus learned return
concepts.description: The plotted training statistic and the discounted value estimate are related but not identical quantities.
concepts.subtopic: Undiscounted logged total versus learned return

concepts.title: One exploration-rate decay
concepts.description: The multiplicative schedule gradually reduces exploration until the floor becomes active.

concepts.title: When the exploration floor first activates
concepts.description: Taking logarithms gives n≥ln(0.1)/ln(0.998)≈1150.14, so the first integer update is 1,151.
concepts.subtopic: When the exploration floor first activates

concepts.title: Logging cadence and averaging window
concepts.description: The first print happens when ep=499, after 500 episodes; the statistic uses the trailing 100 totals.

concepts.title: Reading the printed checkpoint table
concepts.description: An overall favorable trend can contain worse checkpoints. The printed run is not evidence of monotonic improvement.

concepts.title: Unseeded output is not an exact promise
concepts.description: The deterministic epsilon schedule can reproduce while stochastic reward means differ. The author run records versions and explicitly does not claim an identical trace.
concepts.subtopic: Unseeded output is not an exact promise

concepts.title: Valid convolution length
concepts.description: Valid mode includes only positions where the entire 50-value kernel overlaps the data.

concepts.title: What plotted index zero represents
concepts.description: The x label says Episode, but implicit indices are window indices. To place values at window-end episodes, explicit x coordinates would be needed.

concepts.title: What the displayed curve establishes
concepts.description: The plotted statistic is smoothed training return under a still-exploratory behavior policy, not a mathematical convergence or real-world grasp certificate.

concepts.title: Increasing all three grid axes
concepts.description: Tabular storage grows with the Cartesian product of all state-axis sizes and the action count.

concepts.title: Changing shape does not change the encoder
concepts.description: Grid resolution changes require coordinated updates to table shape and encoder bounds; merely enlarging Q leaves added cells inaccessible.
concepts.subtopic: Changing shape does not change the encoder

concepts.title: Range-preserving twelve-bin encoder and saturation
concepts.description: Preserving the 0.32 m nominal span requires w=0.32/12 m and the same 0.16 m offset. Ideal scaled coordinates are 0,6,12; clipping to0…11 gives 0,6,11. Bin0 absorbs the lower tail and bin 11 the upper tail. Interior bin k spans [−0.16+kw,−0.16+(k+1)w); the upper bin begins at e=2/15 m.

concepts.title: What replacing a table with a network changes
concepts.description: Avoiding explicit tabulation can improve representational scaling without eliminating all dimensionality and learning challenges.
concepts.subtopic: What replacing a table with a network changes

concepts.title: Making a real grasping extension
concepts.description: The source’s proposed gripper extension is conceptual. The actual blocked-gripper reaching environment cannot acquire grasping through an action-array edit alone.

concepts.title: One complete encoded transition
concepts.description: The successor Euclidean distance is 0.03 m, so dense reward is−0.03. The greedy branch selects action 0 from tied zeros. Encoding the successor gives (3,4,4), while the old pair is updated to 0+0.1(−0.03+0.95×0−0)=−0.003 before advancing state.

concepts.title: Exploration does not vanish at the floor
concepts.description: The floor creates persistent exploratory behavior, and branch probability differs from actual non-greedy probability.
concepts.subtopic: Exploration does not vanish at the floor

concepts.title: Greedy with an estimate versus greedy with Q*
concepts.description: Do not substitute an unverified current estimate for the true optimal value function in a theorem about greedy optimality.
concepts.subtopic: Greedy with an estimate versus greedy with Q*

concepts.title: Zero initialization with nonpositive reward
concepts.description: Initialization and learning interact with exploitation, but optimism alone does not establish optimality or sufficient exploration.

concepts.title: Environment lifecycle versus visualization
concepts.description: The environment API separates initialization and interaction from display. The source training loop receives observation/info from reset and five outputs from step. Rendering the task is not the same operation as plotting accumulated rewards, and neither implies a Q update by itself.

concepts.title: Extra samples and residual exploration
concepts.description: The extension adds 15,000×50=750,000 steps. Exploration is entered with probability 0.05, but one of its six uniform actions is still greedy, so the non-greedy probability is 0.05×5/6=1/24. The expectation is 31,250 non-greedy choices. More samples alone do not prove convergence, adequate state coverage or optimality.
